name: Bharat Electronics Ltd
about: Incorporated in 1954, Bharat Electronics Ltd manufactures and supplies electronic equipment and systems to the defence sector. Company also has a limited presence in the civilian market [1]

context.speaker: Manoj Jain
context.text: Thank you. So I will just briefly summarize the financial highlights for H1, means Q1 plus Q2 combined for the years '26-'27. The revenue from operations increased to INR12,824 crores up to Q2 as compared to INR10,180 crores with a growth of 25.97%. The profit before tax has also increased to INR3,467 crores up to Q2 as compared to INR3,023 crores with a growth of 14.66%. The profit after tax has increased to INR2,589 crores up to Q2 as compared to INR2,255 crores previous year up to the same time with a growth of 14.80%. The EBITDA up to Q2 is 27.43%. The earnings per share has increased to INR3.54 up to Q2 as compared to INR3.09. The order book position as on 01/10/2026 is INR68,717 crores, and orders Page 2 of 32 Bharat Electronics Limited November 03, 2026 acquired until 1/10/2026 in this financial year, till now, is INR7,334 crores. So that is a brief financial highlights of H1, which includes Q1 and Q2 combined. That is a brief from my side.

context.speaker: Mahesh Raut
context.text: This is Mahesh Raut here from Nomura. Congrats on a very good strong operating performance in second quarter FY27. My first question is pertaining to Next Generation Corvette. Given that the contract was now signed with GRSE and Goa Shipyard yesterday, how soon we can expect a subsystem level awarding for advanced sort of weapons, sensors and navigations for you? And whether that awarding will happen on a competitive route or a nomination base? And given that I think now total ordering contract size has increased from about INR38,000 crores to INR53,000 crores. Do we anticipate incremental changes in terms of ordering size for us? Page 4 of 32 Bharat Electronics Limited November 03, 2026

The first question is on QRSAM. Sir, given there has been a delay, is it possible that the actual size of the order could be greater than INR30,000 crores? Because I understand the INR30,000 crores number was first spoken more than a year back and costs have increased in the interim. Is that how it may play out? Yes.

Generally, we also wish like that, that they give us escalations after the conclusion of price. But typically, as a government process, 1 year, 1.5 years escalations, they don't give. Until, because of various reasons, the project delays too much, and we have to absorb that. So mostly, we may not get any escalation, maybe barring if we are lucky, maybe some 6 months escalation, if they clear very good, that will be a Page 22 of 32 Bharat Electronics Limited November 03, 2026 positive news for you and me. But as of now, I'm expecting INR30,000 crores order to come to us.

So that correction also we wanted to do instead of loading ourselves in the last quarter and then having suspenses for all of you also. We wanted to make it more uniform. So it is more of a correction of that as well as our fast execution speed. We don't want to delay now. Whatsoever delivery commitments are there. We wanted to extend 1 or 2 months this side only. We don't want to go to another side. And we are putting all our efforts to see that our execution track record closes to 100% as early as possible.

So anyway, when big, big orders are there, it takes its own time for the decision-makers also. So they have to sit together for each project one by one. So we are hopeful in next years, we may get positive surprise. So we are not alarmed by the delays right now. And anyway, as I told, we are compensating some of the delay by doing some advanced action for the FOPM realization for which we have done some good proactive investments related to QT and related to realizing this with our supply chain partners also.

So that itself is a very, very good news for all of us that, yes, in this program also, it is, again, a good model of a public-private partnership where in this, the private sector, maybe around 200-plus MSME partners will be there and roughly around 70% of the orders which we are getting will be distributed across these 200-plus MSME partners. And right now, they have done reasonably good investment from their side also. So based on this good ecosystem and good confidence they have on all of us, I am hopeful that this few months delay in acquiring order will not translate into execution.

Yes, hi. Good evening, everyone, and thanks for the opportunity. Couple of questions from my side. The first one is with respect to order inflow that we have witnessed in this Q1 – in this quarter. If I compare it with Q1 FY26 and Q1 FY25, the order inflow has been pretty lean. Just wanted to understand the reasons for that, whether you see a more structural component to it or it is just, the timing of the orders. Just wanted to get a little bit more understanding on that and also QRSAM order which seems to have been delayed? That is my first question, sir.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: FY27 revenue growth of 15%+, held unchanged across Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27 and Q2 FY27 (G25, G9, G1).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Revenue grew 24.9% and 26.5% YoY in Q1 and Q2, 25.8% for H1. Management says it has pulled deliveries forward to avoid a Q4-loaded year (C6), so H2 needs only about 8.6% growth to meet the guide.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: EBITDA margin around 28% for FY27 (G2, G8), softened from 'more than 28%' in Q4 FY26 (G26).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Q2 margin was 27.9% against 29.4% a year earlier, and H1 was 26.6% computed (27.43% per management). H1 PAT grew 14.8% against revenue growth of 26%, so faster execution is diluting margins.

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Management is 'not alarmed by the delays' and still expects INR50,000+ crore of FY27 orders including QRSAM (C7, G3).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: INR7,334 crore was booked in H1, against INR12,824 crore of H1 revenue: a book-to-bill of about 0.57. The target has already been cut from INR55,000+ crore (G27, G7), and QRSAM has been described as delayed since Q1 FY27 (C9).

narrative_vs_numbers.claim: Order delays will not hit execution because of advance action and MSME supply-chain investment (C7, C8).
narrative_vs_numbers.reality: Cash-conversion cycle lengthened from 261 to 342 days over three years and 5-year CFO/PAT is 0.59, consistent with working capital tied up ahead of billing. Whether the advance action converts to revenue is too early to tell.

bull.point: Revenue is compounding ahead of guidance: up 25.8% in H1 FY27 against a 15% guide, after 16.2% in FY26 against 15%. TTM revenue is INR30,253 crore.

Visibility: the INR68,717 crore order book covers 2.3x TTM revenue before QRSAM (about INR30,000 crore, C5) and NGC (about INR20,000 crore, G6) are added; the NGC shipyard contracts are already signed (C3).
Balance sheet and returns: net cash with debt/equity of 0.0 and INR85 crore of borrowings, ROCE 36%, 5-year FCF INR8,376 crore, and margin up 610 bps over three years.

bear.point: Order inflow is behind: INR7,334 crore booked by 1 Oct against a FY27 guide already cut from INR55,000+ crore to INR50,000+ crore. Hitting it needs about INR42,700 crore in H2, and QRSAM has slipped for two quarters.

Margin slippage: Q2 margin was 27.9% against 29.4% a year earlier, and H1 PBT grew 14.66% against revenue growth of 25.97%. QRSAM is priced at a figure first quoted more than a year ago with no escalation expected (C4, C5), so cost inflation falls on BEL.
